Permission; as sought for; stands granted.
He shall file his Vakalatnama before the Registry.
Registry shall accept the same.

sentences.text:
Considering the issue involved in the present application and with consent of the learned advocates appearing for the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14453/2023 ORDER DATED:
18/08/2023 undefined respective parties as well as considering the fact that the dispute amongst the applicant and complainant-victim has been resolved amicably, this matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

3. By way of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "the Code"), the applicant has prayed for quashing and setting aside FIR being C.R.No. 11186008230370 OF 2023 registered with Una Police Station, District Gir Somnath for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code; proceedings of Sessions Case No. 9 of 2023 pending before the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Gir Somnath as well as other consequential proceedings arising therefrom.

entities.text: Una Police Station, District Gir Somnath
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the respective parties submitted that during pendency of the criminal proceedings, as referred to above, the applicant and complaint/victim have amicably settled their issue by way of mutual settlement and pursuant to understanding arrived at, the Complainant/victim has accordingly filed her affidavit, which is on record.

The complainant/victim has categorically stated in the affidavit that dispute is amicably resolved and has no objections if the present proceedings are quashed and there is no surviving grievance between them.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14453/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/08/2023 undefined 5.
Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties, considering the facts and circumstances arising out of the present application as well as taking into consideration the decisions rendered in the cases of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, Nikhil Merchant Vs.
Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 31, Manoj Sharma Vs. State &
Ors., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 190 and Narinder Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported in 2014 (2) Crime 67 (SC), it appears that further continuation of criminal proceedings in relation to the impugned FIR against the applicant would be unnecessary harassment to the applicant.

sentences.text: It appears that the trial would be futile and further continuance of the proceedings pursuant to the impugned FIR would amount to abuse of process of law and Court and hence, to secure the ends of justice, the impugned FIR and other consequential proceedings are required to be quashed and set aside in exercise of powers conferred under Section 482 of the Code.
7. Resultantly, this application is allowed.

The impugned FIR being C.R.No. 11186008230370 OF 2023 registered with Una Police Station, District Gir Somnath; proceedings of Sessions NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14453/2023 ORDER DATED: 18/08/2023 undefined Case No. 9 of 2023 pending before the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Gir Somnath as well as other consequential proceedings are hereby quashed and set aside qua the present applicant herein.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, Rule is made absolute.
